fake_essex
fake_johannesburg
fake_london

items.title: Add ISA check for circuits with custom calibrations
items.body:
**Description**
Calibration support was dropped with the release of Qiskit 2.0. However, when users of qiskit-ibm-runtime install a version of Qiskit < 2.0.0, they can still submit jobs that contain custom calibrations.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Install qiskit-ibm-runtime with Qiskit version < 2.0, for example via `pip install qiskit-ibm-runtime qiskit==1.4 numpy`
2. Initialize a Qiskit Runtime session and connect to a physical hardware backend (e.g., ibm_kyoto).
3. Construct a QuantumCircuit and include a standard delay instruction on a target qubit.
4. Define a custom qiskit.pulse schedule (e.g., a GaussianSquare pulse with a frequency shift) that represents the non-standard Hamiltonian to be injected.
5. Call qc.add_calibration("delay", [qubit_index], pulse_schedule, [duration]) to bind the payload to the ISA gate.
6. Submit the circuit to SamplerV2. 

**What is the expected feature or enhancement?**
Add a check in the ISA validation to ensure that:
- either users get a warning of the same type as that raised by QPY ("UserWarning: Support for loading pulse gates has been removed in Qiskit 2.0. If `delay` is in the circuit it will be left as an opaque instruction.");
- or they get an error that says that pulses are no longer supported.

**Acceptance criteria**
Step 6 should raise a warning or an error.

items.title: [Wrapper sampler MVP1] Write an implementation of SamplerV2 around Executor
items.body:
### Background
The new `Executor` primitive provides more powerful and efficient tools to interact with a quantum computer. However, the `Sampler` provides a convenient abstraction for users to use. To have the best of both worlds, we want to create a new `SamplerV2` implementation which will utilize the `Executor` under the hood.

### Workplan
The new implementation will initially live side by side with the existing implementation at `qiskit_ibm_runtime.executor.routines.sampler_v2`.

#### Phase 1: Minimal viable implementation
In the first phase, the new sampler will only be able to handle basic PUBs, with no advanced options (Twirling, etc.). It will run the `Executor` (with `CircuitItem`) and results will be converted from `QuantumProgramResult` to `SamplerV2Result`.

- [x] #2583
- [x] #2585

#### Phase 2: Options Support & Feature Parity
In the second phase, we will gradually match the options provided by the existing `SamplerV2`. Twirling options will trigger a `Samplomatic` boxing and building step, and result in a `SamplexItem` to be run via the `Executor`.

- [x] #2586
- [x] #2587
- [x] #2588

#### Future
While outside the scope of this epic, it should be noted that the new implementation opens up avenues for further improvements like accepting pre-boxed circuits.

We expect to eventually deprecate and remove the old implementation of `SamplerV2`.

items.title: [Benchmark] Quantum Volume Depth Test on ibm_fez (156 qubits) - Noise Characterization
items.body:
## Quantum Volume Benchmark: Depth Capability Test on ibm_fez

### Summary
Executed Quantum Volume-style circuits to test ibm_fez (156 qubits) depth capabilities and noise characteristics.

### Test Configuration
| Circuit | Qubits | Target Depth | Transpiled Depth | Heavy Output | Pass |
|---------|--------|--------------|------------------|--------------|------|
| QV-4q | 4 | 4 | 27 | 46.2% | ❌ |
| QV-6q | 6 | 6 | 40 | 45.7% | ❌ |

### Key Findings
- **Heavy output threshold:** 67% required for QV pass
- **Actual performance:** ~46% (below threshold)
- **Transpilation impact:** Depth increases 6-7x (4→27, 6→40)
- **Execution time:** 7-9s per circuit

### Interpretation
Results indicate ibm_fez noise levels prevent QV passing at these configurations, but provide valuable characterization data for:
- Noise-aware circuit design
- Benchmarking comparison across IBM devices
- Transpilation depth analysis

### Reproduction
```python
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit, transpile
from qiskit_ibm_runtime import QiskitRuntimeService, SamplerV2

service = QiskitRuntimeService()
backend = service.backend('ibm_fez')
sampler = SamplerV2(mode=backend)

# 4-qubit test
qc = QuantumCircuit(4, 4)
for _ in range(2):  # 2 layers
    for i in range(0, 3, 2):
        qc.h(i)
        qc.cx(i, i+1)
        qc.rz(0.5, i+1)
        qc.cx(i, i+1)
        qc.h(i)
    qc.barrier()
qc.measure_all()

tqc = transpile(qc, backend, optimization_level=1)
job = sampler.run([tqc], shots=512)
result = job.result()
```

### Files
- Raw data: `qv_results.json`
- Full report: `qv_issue_body.md`

### Notes
This benchmark was executed as part of a quantum bounty program using IBM Quantum Open Plan access. The data is offered for inclusion in IBM's device characterization datasets.

items.title: Feature request: Add job status indicating QPU execution
items.body:
### Describe the problem

I've implemented a script to monitor runtime jobs and cancel them after a certain time to conserve quantum credits. The script polls `job.status()` until it reports `RUNNING` and then starts a two-minute timer.

In one instance, a job containing a shallow 4-qubit circuit was cancelled after approximately 2 minutes and 10 seconds. The job metadata indicated that the cancellation logic worked as intended. However, the QPU usage time indicates 0 seconds of QPU usage. Therefore, the `RUNNING` status does not necessarily imply QPU usage.

[Based on the documentation](https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/docs/en/api/qiskit/qiskit.providers.JobStatus), `RUNNING` appears to be the only state indicating that a job has started processing, but this example suggests that `RUNNING` may include other preparation stages before the QPU begins executing.

### Steps to reproduce

I have not been able to reproduce this behavior consistently.

I ran 24 distinct circuits ranging from 3 to 10 qubits with multiple depths, and they all completed normally within the two-minute window without being cancelled. The 4-qubit circuit that was cancelled in the original run was executed again successfully without hitting the two-minute threshold.

### Expected behavior

It would be helpful to include a feature where a distinct job status exists for the QPU execution phase. This would allow users to isolate QPU usage and track quantum credits more reliably.

### Suggested solution

- Add a new job status such as `EXECUTING_ON_QPU` that is set when the processor actually begins executing circuits.

### Additional Information

- qiskit‑ibm‑runtime version: 0.45.1
- Python version: 3.12.12
- Job ID: d6k7j2633pjc73dmsv2g

items.title: Jobs that trigger max_execution_time are not in final state
items.body:
**Describe the bug**

When a job (RuntimeJobV2) is run against a device using `SamplerV2` or `EstimatorV2`, and mx_execution_time is specified ([via options](https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/docs/en/guides/max-execution-time)), the resulting job returns the status `CANCELLED - RAN TOO LONG`.

Because `CANCELLED - RAN TOO LONG` is not in `JOB_FINAL_STATES` (defined [here](https://github.com/Qiskit/qiskit-ibm-runtime/blob/4bb3ddaf4a628d7679d0fc5a244e3b4cd2fa0f07/qiskit_ibm_runtime/runtime_job_v2.py#L56)), calling `job.in_final_state()` or `job.wait_for_final_state()` or `job.result()` hangs indefinitely.

**Steps to reproduce**

Run this snippet against a backend, `job.wait_for_final_state()` will hang forever.

```
from qiskit.circuit.random import random_circuit
from qiskit import transpile

from qiskit_ibm_runtime import QiskitRuntimeService
from qiskit_ibm_runtime import SamplerV2

service = QiskitRuntimeService()
backend = service.backend("<backend>")

sampler = SamplerV2(mode=backend)

sampler.options.max_execution_time = 10

qc = random_circuit(100, 100, measure=True)
qc = transpile(qc, backend)

job = sampler.run([qc])

job.wait_for_final_state()
```

**Expected behavior**

I expect that `wait_for_final_state` would return once the job reaches max_execution_time limit.

In reality, it hangs forever.

**Suggested solutions**

* `CANCELLED - RAN TOO LONG` can be added to `JOB_FINAL_STATES` (defined [here](https://github.com/Qiskit/qiskit-ibm-runtime/blob/4bb3ddaf4a628d7679d0fc5a244e3b4cd2fa0f07/qiskit_ibm_runtime/runtime_job_v2.py#L56))
* Maybe there is a fix that needs to be made so that the status returns `CANCELLED`?

**Additional Information**

- **qiskit-ibm-runtime version**: 0.45.1
- **Python version**: 3.11.9
- **Operating system**: MacOS

items.body:
**What is the expected feature or enhancement?**

The current flow for developers has been in place for a number of years, and in the meantime alternatives have appeared that provide a more convenient experience for developers. This issue is about taking advantage of those and improving the developer experience, via:

3. Use `pytest` as the test runner, while keeping the test suite agnostic to the runner (so developers can chose the runner of their choice). It provides saner log output, as well as more features (by itself and through plugins) than the standard test runner which we can take advantage of.

`pre-commit` can be run in the rerpo for at least QA checks, `pytest` is run in CI, and `pylint` is no longer used.

* preferring using intermediate `__init__.py` files for re-exporting members
* combination of either using too fine-grained modules (for example, for containing just one class) or too wide modules (in particular, `utils` and similar modules accumulating disparate functionality)
* using top-level `__init__.py` (seemingly) for facilitating user imports

As a side effect, most of the package is imported by `import qiskit_ibm_runtime`, and the risk of circular import trickles into a number of changes into the codebase. This story is about:
* refactoring existing code, aiming to improve maintainability and reduce import cycles
* evaluate the practices in the process, and eventually add some guidelines that help us produce more cohesive modules and a better balance between user convenience / developer overhead / scalability

**What is the expected feature or enhancement?**

**Acceptance criteria**

`SamplerV2` is importable with less levels of nesting.

items.title: Reduce default RuntimeJob status polling interval

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: Exists, but can be done better, faster, or different

items.body:
**What is the expected enhancement?**

The `wait_for_final_status` method polls the `GET /v1/jobs/:id` API every 100ms waiting for a terminal status for a job:

https://github.com/Qiskit/qiskit-ibm-runtime/blob/main/qiskit_ibm_runtime/runtime_job_v2.py#L244

That puts a lot of load on multiple API services in the Quantum Cloud stack, and additional infra resources, e.g. tracing, monitoring, logging.

We'd like to see that hard polling lessened by default for non-session jobs but with a way to opt into faster polling (previous behavior) if desired, like for automated integration tests.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Change the default for non-session jobs to be 500ms or 1s for the polling interval
- Allow the polling interval to be overridden (kwarg on the QiskitRuntimeService instance and/or RuntimeJob and/or env var) with a **floor** value of 100ms
- For Session jobs, leave the polling interval default to be 100ms because we don't want longer polling times to impact wall lock usage calculations on sessions

items.title: Avoid / minimize the number of DeprecationWarnings from qiskit

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: Exists, but can be done better, faster, or different

items.body:
**What is the expected enhancement?**

Currently, the codebase uses a number of features deprecated by Qiskit. This is undesirable by users (who get a `DeprecationWarning` that they cannot act upon, as it is emitted from our usage) and developers (the tests output becomes quite clogged with such warnings, and we risk being caught in an actual feature removal during the upgrade to a Qiskit release).

It would be great to avoid or at least minimize the number of `DeprecationWarnings` emitted during regular usage of the package, by using non-deprecated mechanisms instead. Related issues:
* https://github.com/Qiskit/qiskit-ibm-runtime/issues/2350 - tackling the likely biggest source of deprecation warnings (there is an open PR https://github.com/Qiskit/qiskit-ibm-runtime/pull/2351, with relevant context)
* https://github.com/Qiskit/qiskit-ibm-runtime/issues/2782
* https://github.com/Qiskit/qiskit-ibm-runtime/issues/2034
* https://github.com/Qiskit/qiskit-ibm-runtime/issues/2986
* https://github.com/Qiskit/qiskit-ibm-runtime/blob/0.46.1/test/ibm_test_case.py#L65 - related to the tests, ~I recall there was an in-progress PR touching that line, but I cannot find it~ see https://github.com/Qiskit/qiskit-ibm-runtime/pull/2352. The regular expression `r"^qiskit$`" is currently too restrictive (only top-level `qiskit` considered) and relaxing it might help uncovering more warnings or enforcing action on them.
* CI and  `pytest -v -s` is also a good guide for checking emitted warnings

As an extra item to consider, when replacing usages with non-deprecated alternatives, we should make sure that they are supported by the minimal version of Qiskit supported by the package (`2.2` as of today). This will be easier to check one https://github.com/Qiskit/qiskit-ibm-runtime/issues/2575 is tackled.

**Acceptance criteria**

The number of deprecation warnings emitted by the package is 0 or greatly reduced.

items.title: Stop emitting `IBMFractionalTranslationPlugin` deprecation warning with every transpilation

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: Exists, but can be done better, faster, or different

items.body:
**What is the expected enhancement?**

Every transpilation raises a deprecation warning:
```
eprecationWarning: Since backends now support running jobs that contain both fractional gates and dynamic circuit, IBMFractionalTranslationPlugin is deprecated as of qiskit-ibm-runtime 0.42.0 and will be removed no sooner than 3 months after the release date. Use IBMDynamicFractionalTranslationPlugin instead.
```

**Reproducer**

```python
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit, generate_preset_pass_manager
from qiskit_ibm_runtime import QiskitRuntimeService


service = QiskitRuntimeService()
backend = service.backend("your preferred backend")


circ = QuantumCircuit(2, 2)
circ.cz(0, 1)
circ.measure(0, 0)

pm = generate_preset_pass_manager(backend)
pm.run(circ)
```

**Details**

@jakelishman explains that Qiskit constructs all available plugin objects as part of the plugin search, even if they're not actually accessed or used, and a possible solution may be to defer the warning to the `pass_manager()` method of the stage instead of construction time.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] The code snippet above runs without emitting warnings.

items.title: Add an `EstimatorV2` implementation wrapped around `Executor`

labels.name: feature
labels.description: New feature or addition to the project

type.name: Feature request
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
**What is the expected enhancement?**
We want to create a new `EstimatorV2` implementation that wraps around the `Executor`. The new estimator should support all functionality of the legacy estimator, unless technically not available via the `Executor`. Error mitigation techniques will be imported from an external source, and used seamlessly.

**Acceptance criteria**
A user can replace the legacy estimator with the new implementation as a drop-in replacement.

**Steps**

- **Vanilla estimator** - We start with a vanilla version that doesn't do any error mitigation. This version will live in `qiskit-ibm-runtime`.
- **Error mitigation** - We dispatch according to the options to prepare and postprocess functions which are imported from external sources.

### Summary
We need to add a `prepare` function for the Vanilla estimator use-case (no error mitigation). The function will take in PUBs and relevant options (a small subset of the full options of the estimator) and return a `QuantumProgram`.

items.body:
### Summary
We need to add a post processing function which will take a `QuantumProgramResult` created by running the `QuantumProgram` of #2795, and return a `PrimitveResult` fulfiling the contract of `EstimatorV2`.

items.title: [wrapper estimator] Support mid-circuit measurements
items.body:
### Summary
In the context of the estimator, mid-circuit measurements cause problems, as normal usage of Samplomatic's pass manager will add `ChangeBasis` annotations on them. We need to modify the use of the preset pass manger such that only end-of-circuit measurements are annotated with `ChangeBasis`, while all measurements have `Twirl` annotation if twirling is on.

items.title: Optimize measurements and classical registers to minimize returned data
items.body:
### Summary
Unlike legacy estimator, the new implementation will receive back all measurements data and calculate the expectation values based on it. We need to optimize this, so we minimize the amount of data sent back. Particularly:

- Don't measure all qubits, but just the subset needed for the observables.
- Remove cregs which are not needed (with mid-circuit measurements in play this needs to be done carefully, as we need to measure to a valid creg).

items.title: Add modules for decoders and results

labels.name: feature
labels.description: New feature or addition to the project

type.name: Feature request
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
**What is the expected feature?**

Currently, Results and `ResultDecoder` class are defined mostly in the `utils` module, and in the minority of cases in the specific modules for the corresponding program.

Results are very user facing, as the way for users to interact with the output of a program. `ResultDecoder`s are more internal, but central to the responsibility of converting payloads from the API into usable objects (Results, actually), and are also relatively exposed to users (as optional args to `job.result()`, `service.run()` and other places). Decoders usually have self-contained logic for emitting a Result, and Results are self-contained.

This story is about creating new modules for each, for improving modularization and make exposing Results as part of the interface easy and consistent. For existing programs, it is likely a breaking change, which hopefully can be tackled via keeping re-exports during the deprecation window (and some special attention to the hard-coded noise learner modules in the payloads).

**Acceptance criteria**

Two new top-level modules, one for results and one for decoder, are created.

items.title: Align wrapper estimator's uncertainty estimates with legacy estimator
items.body:
### Summary
When ZNE\PEA are off, legacy estimator returns two measures of the uncertainty (documented [here](https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/docs/en/guides/estimator-input-output)):

- `stds` - the standard error of the estimates across different twirling randomizations.
- `ensemble_standard_error` - the standard error of the estimate treating all shots as a single ensemble.

(with twirling off both measures are the same)

The implementation of #2810 returned as `stds` what's defined here as `ensemble_standard_error`.
